html:
The Guarayos are an Indigenous people of eastern Bolivia, north of the department of Santa Cruz, in forests and savannas between the Grande and Blanco rivers. They speak Guarayu, a language of the Tupi-Guarani branch of the Tupian family.

Franciscan friars set up missions among them in the 1800s, which gathered them into towns that still exist, and most Guarayos today are Roman Catholic. The current population is about 12,000. Their neighbours include the Chiquitano and the Sirionó, and the related Guarasugwe.
